attempts.prompt: Generate an image of an entirely novel tool that could be used for cutting food. Its working part, a sharp, straight blade edge, is what does the task: it must look and work exactly like that familiar part. Everything else, meaning the handle, body, how the parts connect and the overall silhouette, must be an unconventional design with zero resemblance to existing knives. Give the tool an unexpected colour and surface texture or material, chosen so that the working part still does the task just as well (do not remove, shrink, blunt or weaken it). Make the background white and add nothing else to the image. Do not include any food or cutting board. Show no text, numbers, labels, arrows, icons, logos or screens anywhere on the object.

attempts.revised_prompt: Generate a photorealistic image of one entirely novel handheld tool whose shape clearly communicates cutting food by downward slicing. It must not resemble existing knives or look like a surface scraper. Use just two permanently joined parts: a conventional stainless-steel cutting blade and a single sculptural purple grip body. Preserve a substantial, uninterrupted, razor-sharp straight blade edge, with a clearly visible fine bevel on both faces; do not shrink, blunt, weaken or conceal it. Orient this long cutting edge horizontally along the bottom. Leave a deep, thin, smooth metal blade face exposed above the entire cutting edge so the blade can descend well into food without the grip body obstructing it. Replace the elongated perforated body with a compact, asymmetrical folded-wave grip positioned above the middle of the blade, not extending backward from one end. Form this grip as one thick continuous ribbon: a broad convex palm saddle flows into a rounded underside finger curl and then into a short, sturdy neck bonded to the blade's upper spine. The grip's two unequal curled lobes extend sideways in opposite directions, creating an unfamiliar sculptural silhouette rather than a conventional handle. Provide ample open clearance between the gripping surface and the cutting edge, with no supports, feet or surrounding frame reaching down beside the edge. Place the palm saddle directly over the blade's midpoint so downward hand pressure visibly drives the entire edge through food. Use lilac food-safe polymer with a fine sealed satin microtexture for the grip and clean polished steel for the blade. Show a three-quarter view from slightly above that clearly reveals the thin blade, sharp lower bevel, exposed cutting depth and unusual grip geometry. Plain white background, nothing else in the image, no food or cutting board, and no hands. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, icons, logos or screens anywhere.
